title: Building a 10 person unicorn - Max Brodeur-Urbas, Gumloop
talk_summary: Max Brodeur-Urbas describes how Gumloop stays under 10 people via picky product-led hiring, near-zero meetings, and automating internal operations with their own workflow product. It is mostly a hiring/culture talk with little on agent engineering, but a few operational patterns transfer.

takeaways.technique: Automate recurring internal ops as workflows, not ad-hoc agent asks
takeaways.what_they_do: They encode repeatable business processes (pre-meeting research reports, signup-triggered outreach drafts, chatbot-log analysis) as standing workflows rather than relying on agents to improvise each time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we automate basically every part of the business as much as we can. And if there's something we can't automate, then we build features

takeaways.technique: Event-triggered work generation to avoid idle agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Signups and chatbot conversations automatically generate notifications, research, and drafted emails, so work appears without a human dispatching it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every time someone interesting signs up, we get notified uh uh why what they're doing on the platform and also like an email drafted

takeaways.technique: Mine product/agent conversation logs for defect signals
takeaways.what_they_do: A workflow reads 50k/day chatbot messages to surface what users are confused about, feeding product decisions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have a gum loop workflow that reads the chats with the chatbot so that it can tell us what people are confused about

takeaways.what_they_do: They challenge the team to ship a requested feature within a 45-minute timer, accepting it can cause burnout if overused.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what if we put on a timer for 45 minutes and try to ship this feature um, right now
